producer_report.summary: `athena status` now lists each uncited user intervention as open work. The cause was that status only counted interventions and never listed them. `StatusView` has a new `open_interventions` field with id, what, category, job and a next command. Each entry also goes into `next`, and the text output gets a `follow-up` line. An intervention counts as cited when a request job received at or after it names its record id in the request text. The records have no better link: `introspection.intervention` points the other way. I left out interventions Athena records itself when you correct a reading, because the job has already taken them. The next command is `athena ask "<request that addresses intervention ID>"`, which matches the CLI's argument form. The citation rule is documented in a doc comment in `status.rs`, a note on `Intervention` in `records.rs`, a new section in `docs/records.md`, and the changelog. `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` pass, and I ran `cargo fmt --all`. Three new tests: two in `lifecycle.rs` (listed with id, category and next command; then dropped once a later request cites the id) and one CLI binary test in `introspection.rs` covering the same two steps in text and JSON. I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` separately after formatting."

checks_run.note: run as --quiet; every suite ok, 0 failed, including the 3 new tests

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A new test records an intervention against a landed job and shows `athena status` listing it as open work, with its id, category and a next command. A second new test shows it disappears from open work once a later job's request cites its id.
criteria_check.evidence: lifecycle.rs: status_lists_an_uncited_intervention_as_open_work_with_a_next_command and an_intervention_leaves_open_work_once_a_later_request_cites_its_id; introspection.rs: the_status_command_lists_an_uncited_intervention_and_drops_it_once_cited (runs the binary). All pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The status view has a distinct open-interventions list (id, what, category, next command). Its entries also appear in `next`, so a reader sees what to run without opening records.
criteria_check.evidence: StatusView.open_interventions: Vec<OpenIntervention> {id, what, category, job, next}; status() pushes each into `next`; the first lifecycle test asserts it.

criteria_check.criterion: An intervention cited by a later job is not listed. The rule for 'cited' is documented in a doc comment and in docs where status is described.
criteria_check.evidence: Doc comment on open_interventions in status.rs and on Intervention in records.rs; new section 'Following up an intervention' in docs/records.md; the second test shows the drop.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: clippy with -D warnings finished clean; cargo fmt --all run.

criteria_check.criterion: The existing counts under 'interventions' (by category and class) are unchanged. Status for a repository with no interventions shows no new open work.
criteria_check.evidence: Count code untouched; tests assert interventions_by_category is unchanged and open_interventions is empty (and no 'follow-up' line) before any intervention.

open_issues: I excluded source=observed interventions (reading corrections) as already handled; the user may want them listed too.
Citation needs request received_at >= intervention at, and uses plain substring match on the id.
mistakes: Early Bash calls with tail/grep were denied by policy; I used the cargo-only forms instead.
learnings: Intervention records have no citing field; introspection.intervention points the other way (analysis of an intervention), so request text naming the id is the only link.
Corrections of readings create source=observed interventions automatically.
